notes: Perfect claim overlap (C43, C44) on RNAi knockdown effects. LLM finds functional validation convincing, while peer reviewers request additional mechanistic data on TAF occupancy changes, indicating uncertainty about completeness of evidence.
High overlap (85.7%) on non-canonical TBP/TAF complex claims (C5, C32-C36). Both evaluators accept the biochemical evidence from sedimentation and co-IP as rigorous and convincing.

Strong overlap (66.7%) on selective TAF expression in undifferentiated hESCs (C1, C27, C71, C72). Both accept the multi-method validation (immunoblot, qRT-PCR, ChIP) as convincing. Peer review also includes differentiation claims C2, C28.

Moderate overlap (50%) on overarching conclusion that TAF composition underlies hESC self-renewal (C8, C96). Both accept this high-level interpretive claim as supported by convergent loss- and gain-of-function evidence.
Exact match on C49 (H3K4me3 enrichment in class I promoters). Both accept the statistical finding; peer review only requests presentation improvement, not challenging the result.
Exact match on C50 (alternative promoters in class II genes). Both accept the finding; peer review requests methodological clarification but does not dispute the conclusion.

Strong overlap (47.1%) on ectopic TAF expression causing differentiation (C7, C59-C65). Both accept the gain-of-function evidence as convincing for demonstrating TAF composition importance in pluripotency maintenance.

Moderate overlap (38.5%) on TAF knockdown causing loss of pluripotency (C6, C56-C58, C70). Both accept the loss-of-function evidence as demonstrating functional requirement for TAF composition in hESC maintenance.
Moderate overlap (35.7%) on two-class gene regulation model (C3, C4, C37-C39). Both accept the ChIP-based classification of genes into Class I (TAF3/5) and Class II (all 6 TAFs) as a key finding.
Moderate overlap (26.7%) on genome-wide ChIP-chip validation (C45-C48). Both accept the global analysis confirming the two-class model with high TAF co-occupancy rates.
Limited overlap (25%) on developmental model (C104). Both accept the conceptual framework that TAF composition changes during differentiation are important for pluripotency regulation.

Limited overlap (20%) on RA-induced differentiation and TAF expression (C2, C28). Both accept that differentiation induces expression of previously absent TAFs. LLM groups this separately while peer review combines with undifferentiated state claims.
Claims C73, C74 on mouse vs human ESC TAF differences appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for species-specific TAF composition.
Claims C108-C111 on feeder contamination and ENCODE discrepancies appear only in LLM results. LLM identifies methodological concerns not explicitly addressed in peer review.
